title: Locum marketplace connection type
description: A connection type manifest, data only: which mechanisms of the app core it uses (authentication methods, trigger kinds, actions), the fields the person fills, and the MCP servers. The app takes the type id and name from the envelope.

minAppVersion.description: The oldest Locum version that installs this connection type, as x.y.z. Required, at 0.1.168 or newer: no earlier release installs connection types. Raise it when the type uses a method, a reader, a trigger kind or an action that older versions do not have; an older app shows the type as needing an update and keeps the installed one running.

logo.description: Logo key known to the app, or null for the generic icon.

color.description: Brand color without #, for the generic icon.

credentialOptional.description: A server with no reference to the credential counts as authorized.

hosts.description: Hosts that identify the type. With a fixed servers.remote.url, the list must include the host of that server: the app does not install a type whose server is on a host left out. Public DNS names only.

aliases.description: Names other tools give to the server of the type.

packages.description: Package names (without version) of stdio servers that belong to the type.

methods.description: How an instance authenticates, in the order the screen offers them.

fields.description: The form an instance fills, besides its name.

healthCheck.description: Up to three GETs that the instance test makes on the base of the remote server (the value of urlField, or servers.remote.url), and the fields of the JSON answer to show. Only with servers.remote.

triggers.description: Trigger kinds of the app core that read this connection, or that read one of its servers (mcp-poll).

actions.description: Flow actions of the app core that need this connection, as <type id>.<action>.

trackers.description: Tracker kinds that live in this connection.

writeTools.description: MCP tools of the servers that write outside the machine. The install screen lists them.

header.description: Header that carries the credential to the remote server.

env.description: Environment variable that carries the credential to the local server.

then.description: The credential of another command line tool, read when needed by a reader in the app code.

The session the person already has in a browser or an app, read by a reader in the app code, and the set of tools the app serves on top of it (`tools`, an id the app registers; one it does not know loses only this method). Cookie, domain, command and code live in the app, never here.

help.description: A line under the field, shown as plain text.

placeholder.description: Hint shown in the empty field, like the default address. Never saved as the value.

path.description: Path added to the end of the base: relative, starting with /, without . or .. segments, scheme, host, query, fragment or markers.

healthCheckField.description: A field of the JSON answer, at the first level, with the label the screen shows.

servers.description: The MCP servers of the type: a remote https endpoint and, when there is one, a local server pinned by digest or lockfile. Never a command.

url.description: Fixed https address on a public host. ${field:<key>} brings the value of a declared field, only in the path: after the first / that follows the host and before ? or #.

urlField.description: Key of the url field the person fills, for a server whose address is per instance.

path.description: Suffix added to the address of urlField, as /mcp: the person types the base address. Only with urlField, without markers or . and .. segments.

headers.description: Headers sent to the server. ${credential} goes only here or in the env of a local server; ${field:<key>} brings the value of a declared field.

image.description: Container image pinned by digest, without a tag.

args.description: Arguments for the server, placed after the image or the bin by the app. Never the credential.

npmPackage.description: An npm package that Locum installs in its own folder from the lockfile, with integrity for every entry.

lockfile.description: The package-lock.json (version 2 or 3) of a project whose only dependency is name@version.
